pr_title: notifier: fix drop alertmanager on apply config step
pr_body:
When the config is applied, set of alertmanagers are recreated with an empty list of URLs (`ams []alertmanager` [init alertmanagerSet](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/notifier/notifier.go#L655)). Before reload will happen, `sendAll` will skip the notification batch, because alertmnager list is empty ( [skip for](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/notifier/notifier.go#L522) ). I think it is necessary to save the list of alertmanagers when applying the config, since it will be updated at the next reload step. 

A test case is added to demonstrate issue above.

Fixes https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/13064

In our cases, we observe that metric prometheus_notifications_dropped_total increases and heartbeat notifications in alertmanager are skipped, this fix repare this.
pr_comments:
We already have a proper fix for this, which is the command line flag `--enable-feature=new-service-discovery-manager`.

Can you please try it?

@roidelapluie 
I posted a comment in issue. Can we discuss about this in issue?

@roidelapluie any news?

This bug can't be fixed with new service discovery and it looks important enough to me as users lose some alerts just because of config reload.
I need to continue testing this. I have started already.
I think this is fixed by https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/14174

I don't think https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/14174 was meant to fix this, the `TestReApplyConfig` added here is still failing on main.

I'll try to revive this with the fix I proposed here https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/13119#discussion_r1646384092

we can close this as https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/14987 was merged.
Thanks again for looking into this.

issue_context.title: Empty activeAlertmanagers list
issue_context.body:
### What did you do?

Empty activeAlertmanagers list after executing reload method (0.001...5 sec)
1 Run prometheus with params (go run cmd/prometheus/main.go --config.file=config.yaml --web.enable-lifecycle)
config.yaml:
```yaml
alerting:
  alertmanagers:
  - http_sd_configs:
    - refresh_interval: 20s
      url: http://xxx/
    timeout: 1m
```
2 make request ```curl -sXPOST http://localhost:9090/-/reload```
3 and then you can try to open ```curl -s http://localhost:9090/api/v1/alertmanagers```
4 Output will be empty. looks like:
```{ "status": "success", "data": { "activeAlertmanagers": [], "droppedAlertmanagers": [] } }```
5 Only after executing peace of code prometheus will update the content of config.
Also reproduced on the main branch. refs:
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/notifier/notifier.go#L310
^
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/discovery/legacymanager/manager.go#L229-L255
^
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/discovery/legacymanager/manager.go#L97

as a result, prometheus has a time window from 0.0001 to 5 seconds when downtime is possible

### What did you expect to see?

```{ "status": "success", "data": { "activeAlertmanagers": [<<<filled data>>>], "droppedAlertmanagers": [] } }```

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

```{ "status": "success", "data": { "activeAlertmanagers": [], "droppedAlertmanagers": [] } }```

### System information

Linux 6.1.0-1012-oem x86_64

### Prometheus version

```text
prometheus, version 2.41.0 (branch: HEAD, revision: 3a097eb28e93d03b8af68bf8d0f4266e81be67d8)
  build user:       root@runner-375ab436-project-7748-concurrent-0bmfc7
  build date:       20230706-12:16:34
  go version:       go1.19.10
  platform:         linux/amd64
```


### Prometheus configuration file

```yaml
alerting:
  alertmanagers:
  - http_sd_configs:
    - refresh_interval: 20s
      url: http://xxx
    timeout: 1m
```

comments:
I don't think the reload should wait for the alertmanagers discovery to finish, as I don't think an alertmanager being down should prevent the user from changing the config of other alertmanagers or any other config.

Plus an alertmanager may disappear just after its discovery, we cannot guarantee it will stay active after the reload, so I don't see why the reload should wait for that.

I see the verifications that run during the reload as a way to detect bugs at compilation, what happens at runtime should be dealt with by other components/mechanisms.

We already have a proper fix for this, which is the command line flag `--enable-feature=new-service-discovery-manager`.

Can you please try it?

Ah, this is not what I understood, I though the issue was about the **first** discovery of alertmanagers being done after the reload (which is not an issue for me).

But the transient disappearance of alertmanagers during a reaload, this is indeed an issue.

 I made a test with `--enable-feature=new-service-discovery-manager` and I'm not sure it helps, I think @tommy0 already has a unit test in the PR to confirm that.

Our prometheus instancses already work with flag `--enable-feature=new-service-discovery-manager` and this behavior was reproduced there. I also ran code from master prometheus local with this flag and reproduce this bug.

I think config reolad does not depends of new discovery. Yeah, can you see unit test in the PR ?

review_comments:
I don’t think we should rely on `k` for this, given how it’s constructed: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/5c417684f87f2e7f55b172b3e5e5c96ac9bc2e2c/config/config.go#L910-L917. It only takes the config position in the array into account. Reordering the configs or changing the entire SD config for an entry may temporarily mess with its `ams` which isn't desired.

I'd expect a test case for that as well.

I think we'll need to compare the configs as we do in other places. If the `AlertmanagerConfig` is already known, temporarily use the corresponding `alertmanagerSet`'s `ams`.

We'll need to agree on certain behaviors:
- Should we set the existing `droppedAms` as well?
- Perhaps we don't want the entire `AlertmanagerConfig` to be the same. Maybe equal `ServiceDiscoveryConfigs` (and `RelabelConfigs`) are sufficient, but it wouldn't be safe.
